column3: Close to the Hebrew.
“Great” is rendered “rich.” NASB carries the sentence through a parenthesis (verse 3) into verse 4.
NASB places the verse in parentheses; “good of insight” is rendered “intelligent,” and “hard” as “harsh.”
Close to the Hebrew; NASB opens with “that,” completing the sentence begun in verse 2.
“Ask him in my name about welfare” is rendered “greet him in my name.”
“To the living one” is rendered “Have a long life”; the meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain.
“Humiliated” is rendered “insulted.”
“A good day” is rendered “a festive day,” and “what your hand finds” as “whatever you find at hand.” NASB supplies “my” before “young men.”
“They rested” is rendered “they waited.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“My slaughter” is rendered “my meat,” and “who I do not know from where they are” as “whose origin I do not know.”
“Turned round to their way” is rendered “retraced their way.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“To bless our master” is rendered “to greet our master,” and “he shouted at them” as “he scorned them.”
“Humiliated” is rendered “insulted.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“A son of worthlessness” is rendered “such a worthless man.”
“Seahs” is rendered “measures,” and “jars” as “jugs.”
“Servants” is rendered “young men.”
“The cover of the mountain” is rendered “the hidden part of the mountain.”
Close to the Hebrew.
NASB follows the Hebrew “to the enemies of David.” “One who urinates on a wall” is rendered “one male.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“On me, my lord, the iniquity” is rendered “On me alone, my lord, be the blame”; NASB adds “alone.”
“Set his heart to” is rendered “pay attention to,” and “disgraceful folly” as “folly.”
“Coming in bloods” is rendered “shedding blood,” and “delivering your hand to you” as “avenging yourself by your own hand.”
“This blessing” is rendered “this gift,” and “who go about at the feet of” as “who accompany.”
Close to the Hebrew; “from your days” is rendered “all your days.”
“And a man has arisen” is rendered “should anyone rise up,” and NASB adds “as from” before “the hollow of a sling.”
Close to the Hebrew.
